parts.title: Trouble at Miller's Creek
parts.text: Imani had always loved Miller's Creek, but this spring something was wrong. Where the water once rushed over smooth stones, it now sat **stagnant** and green, smelling like old eggs. Carter pointed at the pipes beside the parking lot. After every storm, **runoff** from the pavement carried oil and litter into the stream, and thick gray **sediment** had buried the pebbles where minnows used to hide. "If this continues, the mud and chemicals will **contaminate** everything downstream," he warned.

parts.title: Testing the Water
parts.text: Yara, who dreamed of studying **ecology**, brought testing kits from her science class. The results made her gasp: the creek held traces of a **toxic** cleaner, dangerous to fish and frogs. Worse, the creek flowed into the town's **reservoir**, where thousands of families got their drinking water. The students suspected that the nearby car wash had been **negligent**, ignoring the rules about draining its waste.

parts.title: A Plan for the Creek
parts.text: At the next town meeting, the three friends presented their data and urged adults to **conserve** the creek instead of ignoring it. Without action, the habitat would continue to **degrade**, one dead fish at a time. Volunteers agreed to **reclaim** the banks by hauling away trash, planting reeds to filter the water and sealing the leaking drain. Imani described the clear, **pristine** creek her grandfather remembered and promised that she would see it again.

parts.title: Back to the Water
parts.text: By midsummer, minnows flickered through the shallows once more, and a heron stood on the bank. Carter kept a notebook of the changes, while Yara mailed the results to the state office. Imani sat on a warm rock, listening to the water, and understood that one small group can protect a place.

definitions.meaning1: To make something dirty or unsafe by adding harmful substances. Example: Spilled paint can contaminate a stream and harm the fish.

definitions.meaning1: Tiny pieces of sand, mud or rock that settle at the bottom of water. Example: After the flood, a thick layer of sediment covered the riverbed.

definitions.meaning1: To protect something and use it carefully so it is not wasted or destroyed. Example: We turn off the faucet while brushing our teeth to conserve water.
definitions.studentChallenge: Hikers must ___ their drinking water on the long, dry trail.

definitions.meaning1: To make something worse in quality or condition. Example: Years of pollution began to degrade the quality of the lake.
definitions.meaning2: To break down into smaller parts over time. Example: Plastic bags can take hundreds of years to degrade.
definitions.studentChallenge: Heavy traffic and dust can ___ the air quality of a city.

definitions.meaning1: To make damaged land useful again, or to take back something that was lost. Example: Volunteers worked to reclaim the polluted lot and turn it into a garden.
definitions.meaning2: To ask for or take back what belongs to you. Example: You can reclaim your lost backpack at the front office.
definitions.studentChallenge: The city plans to ___ the old dump and turn it into a park.

definitions.meaning1: Poisonous and harmful to living things. Example: Never mix cleaning sprays, since the fumes can be toxic.
definitions.meaning2: Extremely harmful in a way that is not physical. Example: A toxic argument can damage a friendship for years.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ chemical was kept in a locked cabinet far from children.

definitions.meaning1: Rainwater or melted snow that flows over the ground into streams, often carrying dirt and pollution. Example: Farm runoff carried fertilizer into the nearby pond.
definitions.studentChallenge: Heavy rain sent muddy ___ rushing down the hillside.

definitions.meaning1: Not moving or flowing, so that it becomes dirty or smelly. Example: Mosquitoes breed in stagnant puddles.
definitions.meaning2: Not growing, changing or improving. Example: Sales were stagnant all year, so the shop owner tried new ideas.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ pond was thick with algae and buzzing with flies.

definitions.meaning1: Perfectly clean and unspoiled, as if untouched. Example: The hikers camped beside a pristine mountain lake.
definitions.studentChallenge: Fresh snow covered the field in a ___ white blanket.

definitions.meaning1: A large natural or artificial lake where water is stored for a community. Example: The city's reservoir was nearly empty after the long drought.
definitions.meaning2: A large supply of something. Example: She had a reservoir of patience that never seemed to run dry.
definitions.studentChallenge: Pipes carried water from the ___ to every home in town.

definitions.meaning1: Failing to give proper care or attention to something you are responsible for. Example: The negligent owner forgot to lock the gate, and the dog escaped.
definitions.studentChallenge: A ___ lifeguard who watches a phone instead of the pool puts swimmers at risk.

definitions.meaning1: The study of how living things relate to each other and to their surroundings; also, those relationships themselves. Example: Studying the pond's ecology showed how frogs, insects and plants depend on one another.
definitions.studentChallenge: In ___ class, we studied how wolves change a whole forest.
